To help us get to our future, we’re looking for forward thinkers, people with big ideas, people passionate about technology and most importantly hard working team players to join us and be a part of our growing business. Job purpose: The Systems Administrator will be responsible for the day-to-day management, security, maintenance and compliance of the organisation's internal infrastructure platforms. Be part of project teams as required to renew current systems and deploy new solutions. Ensure that all internal infrastructure remains secure, supported, patched and compliant with the organisation's security policies and UK Telecommunications Security Act (TSA) requirements. See Regulation 12 / Chapter 11 – Patching & Updates of the TSA supporting the o organisation's ongoing external security and TSA audits as required. Diagnose, troubleshoot and resolve software, hardware and infrastructure-related network issues, working with Network Engineering and Network Operations teams as appropriate. Ensure that operating systems, applications, infrastructure platforms and supporting services are maintained with current security patches, vendor bug fixes and security updates. This is a proactive, hands-on role focused on preventing security and compliance issues rather than simply responding to them. What you’ll be doing: Proactive Systems Administration Install, configure and maintain software, hardware and operating system features and policies in support of the Network Engineering and Operations function. Ensure proper and secure storage, backup and retrieval of systems and data. Identify areas for improvement, end-of-life notifications and other systems issues. Assist the Network Operations Centre on complex/pervasive problems. Replacement of failed components on-site as required. Ensure that documentation is updated according to company requirements. TSA, Security & Compliance Own the operational infrastructure activities required to maintain compliance with UK Telecommunications Security Act (TSA) requirements and associated security obligations. Ensure operating systems, applications and infrastructure platforms receive security patches, vendor bug fixes and firmware/software updates within agreed timescales and defined security and hardening standards. Monitor vendor security advisories and vulnerability notifications and assess their relevance and impact. Identify and remediate vulnerabilities across the infrastructure estate based on risk and defined remediation SLAs. Ensure infrastructure remains within supported vendor versions and identify end-of-life or unsupported systems. Work closely with the Security, Network Technology and IT teams to identify and address security risks. Support security incident investigations and remediation where infrastructure is involved. Ensure appropriate logging, monitoring and alerting is implemented across managed infrastructure. Maintain secure configuration baselines and ensure systems remain aligned with them.
